note: The discipline library. Every 'why' is one sentence stating a mechanism, never encouragement. This file ships with the app and is never fetched.

items.title: Clear one surface
items.why: A clear surface changes how the whole room reads, which makes it the cheapest visible win in the flat.

items.title: The dishes
items.why: Starting is the expensive part, and a sink you can see the bottom of stays empty longer.

items.title: One drawer
items.why: A drawer is small enough to finish in one sitting, which is what separates it from tidying the room.

items.title: Put the clean pile away
items.why: Clean laundry that never gets put away charges you the same decision every morning.

items.title: Change the sheets
items.why: It is a ten minute job that gets postponed for weeks, and the payoff lands the same night.

items.title: Clear one fridge shelf
items.why: Food you are avoiding looking at is food you are not going to cook.

items.title: Find ten things to bin
items.why: A fixed number turns an open-ended declutter into something with an end.

items.title: Clear the floor of one room
items.why: Floor space is what your eye reads as mess, well before anything on the shelves.

items.title: Walk with no destination
items.why: Twenty minutes outside changes how the evening feels, and it removes the step of deciding where to go.

items.title: Stretch on the floor
items.why: Ten minutes undoes a little of what eight hours in a chair did.

items.title: Twenty push-ups
items.why: Short enough that the excuse has to be an honest one.

items.title: One album, one kitchen
items.why: Pairing a chore with music you like makes the chore the price of the music.

items.title: Stairs
items.why: No equipment and no commute, and it works whether you have ten minutes or thirty.

items.title: Fill the water bottle
items.why: Most of not drinking water is not having any within reach.

items.title: Start going to bed
items.why: The hard part is not sleeping, it is stopping, and stopping is a task like any other.

items.title: Get outside before noon
items.why: Morning light is the cheapest input to sleeping properly tonight.

items.title: Sit with no phone
items.why: Ten minutes with nothing to look at is uncomfortable, and the discomfort is the exercise.

items.title: Read a real book
items.why: A book you have to hold competes with nothing else for your hands.

items.title: Write five lines about today
items.why: Five lines is short enough that you will do it and long enough to show a pattern over a month.

items.title: Plan tomorrow
items.why: Deciding tonight makes tomorrow morning execution rather than negotiation.

items.title: Close the tabs
items.why: An unread tab is a decision you already made and are still paying for.

items.title: Write down what is bothering you
items.why: A worry on paper has a specific size; a worry in your head does not.

items.title: Name the thing you are avoiding
items.why: Writing it down costs nothing and is often the whole blockage.

items.title: Phone in another room
items.why: Distance works where willpower does not, because the phone has to be fetched.

items.title: The email you are avoiding
items.why: It is almost always shorter to write than it has been to avoid.

items.title: Book the appointment
items.why: The booking takes five minutes; the postponing has taken months.

items.title: Open the envelopes
items.why: Unopened post does not become less true, and most of it turns out to be nothing.

items.title: Cancel one subscription
items.why: One cancellation keeps paying you back every month with no further effort.

items.title: Back up your phone
items.why: The cost of skipping this is not gradual, it arrives all at once.

items.title: Look at your balance
items.why: Not looking does not change the number, it only delays knowing it.

items.title: Do the update it keeps asking about
items.why: A postponed update becomes a forced update at the worst possible moment.

items.title: Find the document before you need it
items.why: Looking for it now is calm, and looking for it later will not be.

items.title: Instrument
items.why: Twenty minutes a day beats three hours on Sunday, because the hands remember frequency rather than duration.

items.title: The side project
items.why: Half an hour is enough to get back into it, and getting back in is what stops most restarts.

items.title: Ten minutes of the language
items.why: Ten minutes daily is what actually moves a language, and it is small enough to survive a bad week.

items.title: Sketch one object
items.why: Drawing one thing badly is how drawing starts, and it needs no setup.

items.title: Write 200 words
items.why: A word count can be finished in a way that working on the thing cannot.

items.title: Learn one shortcut
items.why: One shortcut a week compounds across every working day you have left.

items.title: Fix the thing that annoys you daily
items.why: A small annoyance charges you attention every day until it is fixed once.

items.title: Tidy the project folder
items.why: A folder you can navigate is the difference between starting next time and not.
